name: Sun Oil

summary.text: Sun Oil Company (later Sun Company, now Sunoco) was founded by Joseph Newton Pew; his son J. Howard Pew was president from 1912 to 1947. The Pew family's charitable funds, set up from 1948, held Sun Company stock until 1997. Kruse's account of Spiritual Mobilization names 'Sun Oil President J. Howard Pew' as its principal funder.

sources.title: How 'One Nation' Didn't Become 'Under God' Until The '50s Religious Revival

facts.claim: J. Howard Pew was president of the Sun Oil Company from 1912, on his father's death, until 1947.
facts.quote: When his father died in 1912, he became president of the Sun Oil Company a position he was to hold until 1947.

facts.claim: The Pew Charitable Trusts says the seven family trusts that fund it divested their holdings in Sun Company (Sun Oil Co.) in 1997.
facts.quote: divested their holdings in Sun Company (Sun Oil Co.) in 1997

facts.claim: Kruse identifies 'Sun Oil President J. Howard Pew' as a funder of Spiritual Mobilization; The Nation's summary of his book says the group channeled donations from Pew and tire magnate Harvey Firestone.
facts.quote: Its funders included Sun Oil President J. Howard Pew
